correctness.rationale: For finite connected simple bipartite diameter-four graph of girth≥8, opposite-side distances are at most three and same-side threshold-three adjacency means shared neighbor, giving literal join K3=L_A*L_B. C4-freeness makes neighborhood blocks share at most one vertex; C6-freeness forces all cliques inside a single opposite-neighbor simplex. Coning over blocks yields an expansion that collapses both onto each L and onto G using free faces (σ,σ∪{y}) in descending base-face size for |σ|≥2. Thus each L≃G≃∨^bS¹ and K3≃∨^(b²)S³. Adamaszek (arxiv:1104.0433) Prop2.2 ensures K2 collapses to K1 since girth≥8. At diameter four the complex becomes a simplex. This proves all integer persistence intervals, including scale 1-to-2 isomorphism. Finite independent programs verify all structural conditions and exact mod-two boundary calculations for C8, grid, W2 and W3, and full W2 Rips scales 0..3; these tests are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Complete integral persistence for a structural graph class including every existing finite generalized quadrangle is a natural nontrivial topological invariant, not a numerical exercise. The proof locates the radius-three homology jump in an exact join of two graph-equivalent complexes and yields a square of the graph cycle rank. The family makes the fourth-power law b²=s⁴t⁴ and 6561 spheres for W(3) meaningful general consequences, not extrapolations. It explains all integral persistence maps and torsion-freeness without requiring downstream theorems; limits to girth≥8, bipartiteness and diameter four are explicit.
